paragraphs: This paper studies how token representations change as they pass through the depth of an encoder-only transformer during inference. It treats tokens as interacting particles and analyzes their collective evolution. The object being tracked is the empirical measure of the tokens: a mathematical description of how their representations are distributed, rather than a separate account of every token.

The analysis concerns a specific limit called the moderate interaction regime. The number of tokens becomes large while the model’s inverse temperature parameter grows along with it. Under this scaling, the dynamics unfold at three different rates. First, representations rapidly concentrate in a lower-dimensional space. Next, they form clusters. Finally, those clusters merge sequentially on a slower timescale until one remains.

The authors rigorously characterize the limiting dynamics of each phase and prove convergence in the stated regime, with simulations illustrating the results. The contribution is a mathematical explanation of distinct stages of collective token evolution. Its conclusions concern the modeled inference dynamics and scaling assumptions, rather than an unrestricted claim about every transformer.
neurips-2025-a-multiscale-analysis-of-me.tldr: A mathematical analysis identifies three timescales of token concentration and merging in mean-field transformers under a specified large-token scaling regime.

paragraphs: Running diffusion generation across several accelerators creates a communication problem: devices repeatedly exchange large intermediate activations. CompactFusion starts from the observation that activations at neighboring diffusion steps are highly similar. Sending them in full therefore consumes bandwidth on information that has largely already been communicated, limiting the benefit of distributing computation.

The framework instead transmits compressed residuals, meaning the differences between activations at successive steps. This targets the new information introduced at each step. Lightweight error feedback addresses the accumulation of compression errors. The paper supports this design with empirical analysis and theoretical justification, reporting substantial reductions in transmitted data while maintaining generation fidelity.

On four L20 accelerators, CompactFusion reports a threefold speedup alongside improved fidelity. For communication-heavy sequence parallelism on slow networks, it reports a 6.7-fold speedup over a prior overlap-based method. These results show how exploiting redundancy across diffusion steps can improve distributed serving. The framework is presented as applicable across models and parallel configurations, with integration that does not require redesigning the serving pipeline.
neurips-2025-accelerating-parallel-diffu.tldr: CompactFusion accelerates distributed diffusion inference by communicating compressed changes between steps instead of repeatedly sending similar activations.

paragraphs: Strong mathematical accuracy does not by itself establish whether a language model produces creative solutions. This paper addresses the separate problem of assessing creativity in mathematical reasoning. The authors identify two obstacles: defining what counts as creativity and avoiding dependence on human evaluation whenever a generated solution needs to be assessed.

CLAWS defines and classifies solutions into three categories: Typical, Creative, and Hallucinated. It uses attention weights linking sections of the prompt and the generated output as evidence for that classification. Because these signals come from inside the model, the method assesses generation through internal behavior. The distinction between creative and hallucinated solutions is central to the proposed classification.

The evaluation covers 4,545 problems from 181 mathematics contests and five mathematical reasoning models with seven to eight billion parameters. CLAWS outperforms five existing methods that use internal signals, including perplexity, entropy, hidden representations, and attention scores. The findings support attention organized around prompt sections as a useful basis for automated creativity assessment within the mathematical settings studied.
neurips-2025-claws-creativity-detection-.tldr: CLAWS uses attention patterns to classify mathematical solutions as typical, creative, or hallucinated without human evaluation.

paragraphs: Object Goal Navigation asks an agent to find a specified object in an unfamiliar environment. Doing so requires reasoning about parts of the scene it has not observed. The paper argues that deterministic approaches to completing semantic maps overlook uncertainty in indoor layouts, which can restrict how well navigation transfers to new environments.

GOAL addresses this with a generative flow model that learns a distribution over indoor semantic layouts. During training, large language models supply spatial priors, which are represented as two-dimensional Gaussian fields and added to full-scene target maps. The flow model learns to connect observed regions with these enriched maps, absorbing contextual knowledge into its map-completion process.

This design makes uncertainty in unseen regions part of the modeling problem while bringing language-model knowledge into spatial predictions. The reported experiments achieve state-of-the-art performance on MP3D and Gibson and strong transfer to HM3D. Together, those findings support the usefulness of training a generative map model with contextual spatial priors for navigation beyond the environments it originally encounters.
neurips-2025-distilling-llm-prior-to-flo.tldr: GOAL trains a generative flow model with language-model spatial priors to improve unseen-scene completion and object navigation.

paragraphs: The paper considers controlling a linear dynamical system when the controller sees only part of its state and disturbances may be adversarial. A controller must choose actions from incomplete observations while coping with unfavorable external influences. The proposed algorithm, Double Spectral Control, targets efficient learning of the best linear dynamical controllers in this setting.

Its central mechanism is a two-level spectral approximation. The method applies a double convolution using a universal basis of spectral filters, providing a structured way to approximate the dynamics involved in control. The two approximation levels are the key innovation behind the algorithm’s combination of computational efficiency and accurate controller learning.

Double Spectral Control matches the best known regret guarantees while improving runtime dependence on the system’s stability margin by an exponential factor. Regret measures performance relative to the comparison controllers over time. Thus, the stated advance preserves the existing quality of that guarantee while making a particular source of computational difficulty substantially less costly; the exponential improvement specifically concerns stability-margin dependence.
neurips-2025-efficient-spectral-control-.tldr: Double Spectral Control matches leading regret guarantees while exponentially improving runtime dependence on the stability margin for partially observed linear systems.

paragraphs: Composed video retrieval searches for a video using both an example clip and text describing a desired change. Existing benchmarks emphasize appearance or broad event differences, leaving subtle changes in fast movements insufficiently tested. TF-CoVR addresses this gap with gymnastics and diving, where distinguishing closely related actions requires attention to their temporal structure.

The benchmark contains 180,000 triplets from FineGym and FineDiving. An LLM uses label differences between clips from different videos to construct modification requests. Each query and modification has multiple valid targets, averaging 3.9. This supports retrieval situations where several clips can satisfy the request. The proposed model first learns fine-grained action representations, then uses contrastive learning to align composed queries with candidate videos.

The study compares image, video, and general multimodal embedding models with and without fine-tuning. TF-CoVR-Base increases zero-shot mAP@50 from LanguageBind’s 5.92 to 7.51 and the fine-tuned state of the art from 19.83 to 27.22. These results support explicitly learning temporal distinctions before training the retrieval relationship.
neurips-2025-from-play-to-replay-compose.tldr: TF-CoVR introduces a benchmark and two-stage model for retrieving videos through subtle, text-specified changes in sporting movements.

paragraphs: Diffusion image editing often reconstructs an input image and transfers reconstruction features into a generation guided by a new prompt. This helps preserve content, but directly replacing features can create incompatibilities and make structural or pose changes difficult. FSI-Edit studies how to preserve useful image information while allowing the generation to depart from the original arrangement.

Its first mechanism separates features by frequency. It injects high-frequency components from reconstruction features while preserving the ability to change major structures encoded in low-frequency information. Its second mechanism adds controlled noise to the reconstruction features being transferred. This stochastic component expands the range of possible generations, supporting non-rigid edits that would otherwise be constrained by the source image.

Experiments cover edits including object addition, deletion, and pose manipulation. The method outperforms existing baselines in alignment with the target request, semantic fidelity, and visual quality. These findings support treating transferred features selectively: their frequency content and controlled randomness both matter when balancing preservation of the source with flexibility in the requested edit.
neurips-2025-fsi-edit-frequency-and-stoc.tldr: FSI-Edit combines high-frequency feature transfer with controlled noise to make diffusion image edits more flexible while preserving fidelity.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can classify nodes effectively, but incorrect training labels can substantially damage their performance. GD² uses a property specific to graph data to detect this noise: a node has its own features, yet it also belongs to a neighborhood that supplies structural context. Those two sources of information can yield different predictions.

The framework constructs an ego-view from the node’s features and a structure-view by aggregating neighboring representations. It compares their predictions to identify disruptions in the semantic relationship between the node and its surroundings. A further training strategy gives the views differentiated supervision, increasing prediction divergence in a way designed to improve the detection of mislabeled nodes.

Across multiple datasets and noise settings, the authors report better performance than state-of-the-art baselines. The contribution is both a detection signal and a way to strengthen that signal during training. The experiments support using disagreement between individual and neighborhood-based predictions to improve robustness, bringing graph relationships directly into the treatment of unreliable labels.
neurips-2025-gd-2-robust-graph-learning-.tldr: GD² detects noisy graph labels by comparing predictions from a node’s own features with predictions from its neighborhood.

paragraphs: Recognizing objects in three dimensions from a single image requires suitable training annotations. Existing monocular 3D detectors perform well in indoor and driving settings but struggle with more varied images. The paper identifies limited datasets and the difficulty of producing 3D annotations as obstacles to extending this capability to a broader range of objects and scenes.

LabelAny3D uses analysis by synthesis: it reconstructs a holistic 3D scene from a 2D image and uses that reconstruction to produce 3D bounding boxes. This makes scene reconstruction an annotation tool. The authors then apply the pipeline to MS-COCO to create COCO3D, an open-vocabulary monocular 3D detection benchmark containing many categories absent from existing 3D datasets.

Experiments show that the generated annotations improve monocular 3D detection across multiple benchmarks and exceed prior automatic labeling approaches in annotation quality. The findings support foundation-model-driven annotation as a promising route to expanding 3D recognition data. The contribution combines the labeling framework with a benchmark that broadens the object categories available for evaluating detection.
neurips-2025-labelany3d-label-any-object.tldr: LabelAny3D reconstructs scenes from single images to generate 3D boxes and build a broader object-detection benchmark.

paragraphs: Medical vision-language models need paired images and text, but medical datasets are less abundant than natural-image collections. MedicalNarratives draws on educational medical videos from YouTube to expand this training material. Its key observation is that instructors often describe an image while moving a mouse cursor over the relevant region, creating a usable association between spoken explanation and image location.

The dataset contains 4.7 million medical image-text pairs. One million samples include spatial traces and bounding boxes, while 118,000 videos are centered on trace events and paired with aligned text. These annotations connect descriptions to particular image regions and support studying those connections across time, extending the information available beyond isolated image-caption pairs.

To evaluate the dataset, the authors train GenMedClip using a CLIP-like objective across 12 medical domains. On a newly constructed medical imaging benchmark, it outperforms previous state-of-the-art models in all 12 domains. The result supports educational narration and cursor activity as useful sources of supervision for learning medical image and language representations.
neurips-2025-medicalnarratives-connectin.tldr: MedicalNarratives turns educational medical videos, narration, and cursor traces into large-scale supervision linking language to image regions.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning requires repeated interaction with simulated environments, so simulation speed can limit how quickly experiments finish. The paper describes a common bottleneck: environments compute interactions on CPUs, and distributing that work adds communication overhead. Even when model training is accelerated, the supply of experience can remain constrained by environment execution.

NAVIX reimplements MiniGrid in JAX to support fast, batched simulation. MiniGrid is used in research on exploration, curricula, representation learning, credit assignment, and other reinforcement learning questions. Accelerating this shared environment infrastructure therefore supports many kinds of experiments. The central contribution is improving the throughput of the environments that generate training experience.

In batch mode, the authors report speed improvements exceeding 160,000 times and support for up to 2,048 agents in parallel on a single Nvidia A100 with 80 GB of memory. They report reducing experiment duration from one week to 15 minutes. These results illustrate the potential for faster iteration through scalable simulation; the reported throughput figures specifically concern the stated batched setup.
neurips-2025-navix-scaling-minigrid-envi.tldr: NAVIX reimplements MiniGrid in JAX to greatly increase batched simulation throughput and shorten reinforcement learning experiments.

paragraphs: Omni-DNA addresses several demands on genomic models together: understanding DNA sequences, handling long contexts, and describing sequence function in natural language. The authors revisit pretraining architectures and post-training methods to develop a family ranging from 20 million to 1.1 billion parameters. The work also examines adaptation across biologically related tasks.

For long sequences, the paper introduces SEQPACK, which compresses historical tokens into a learned synopsis. A position-aware sampling mechanism determines how that history is represented, allowing transformer models to process very long inputs with low memory and computation requirements. This is relevant to regulatory relationships involving distant sequence regions. The seq2func dataset additionally supports training models to express sequence interpretations in text.

Omni-DNA achieves state-of-the-art results on 18 of 26 evaluations from Nucleotide Transformer and Genomic Benchmarks. Joint fine-tuning on related tasks consistently outperforms existing models. It also improves enhancer-target interaction prediction over distances of 450,000 base pairs. Together with reported meaningful textual annotations, these findings support a genomic modeling approach spanning sequence prediction, distant interactions, and language-based interpretation.
neurips-2025-omni-dna-a-genomic-model-su.tldr: Omni-DNA combines genomic sequence modeling, compressed long-context processing, and natural-language annotation in one model family.

paragraphs: Learning-to-optimize methods train models to provide inexpensive predictions for optimization tasks. Message-passing graph neural networks are one approach, including for linear and quadratic programs. Such models can reduce expensive computations inside larger solvers, but learning robust behavior becomes difficult when training examples are scarce, especially for more complex quadratic problems.

This paper develops data augmentation specifically for quadratic programs. The transformations have theoretical justification and generate varied instances while preserving optimality. That property matters because augmentation must respect the mathematical problem being learned. The authors incorporate these transformed instances into self-supervised contrastive pretraining, giving the graph network a way to learn useful representations before supervised adaptation.

Experiments show improved generalization in supervised learning-to-optimize tasks and effective transfer to related optimization problems. The contribution links a mathematical requirement on augmented problems with a representation-learning strategy. It provides a principled way to obtain more training value from limited problem data, with the reported benefits appearing both when learning the original task and when adapting to related ones.
neurips-2025-principled-data-augmentatio.tldr: Optimality-preserving augmentation and contrastive pretraining improve graph networks that learn to solve quadratic optimization problems.

paragraphs: Quantization reduces the numerical precision used by a model, helping make super-resolution networks more efficient. Video adds complications beyond individual images: errors can propagate over time, parameters are shared across temporal processing, and evaluation measures may not match those temporal effects. QBasicVSR designs quantization around these characteristics of video super-resolution.

Its post-training quantization framework includes flow-gradient video bit adaptation and temporal shared layer bit adaptation. These mechanisms make precision adaptation sensitive to video dynamics and temporally shared computation. The paper also introduces fine-tuning supervised by a full-precision model, using that model as a guide when improving the quantized version.

The authors report up to 200-fold faster processing while using one eighth of the GPU resources, alongside improvements over existing post-training quantization methods. In a stated example, quantizing BasicVSR to four bits with 100 unlabeled video clips yields a 2.53 dB gain on UDM10. The results support addressing temporal behavior explicitly when compressing video models, with the reported gains tied to the evaluated configurations.
neurips-2025-qbasicvsr-temporal-awarenes.tldr: QBasicVSR adapts quantization to video’s temporal behavior to improve the efficiency and quality of low-precision video super-resolution.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation replaces a large training dataset with a small synthetic one. This paper examines why the approach struggles when some classes have many examples and others have few. It focuses on soft labels, which distribute training targets across classes, and shows that their biases are important to understanding performance under such long-tailed distributions.

The authors derive a generalization bound that accounts for imbalance. By systematically changing imbalance levels, they identify two sources of soft-label bias: the model used for distillation and the distilled images themselves. Their Adaptive Soft-label Alignment module, ADSA, calibrates these intertwined biases and can be added to existing distillation pipelines with little overhead.

Experiments report consistent improvements across distillation techniques and under limited label budgets. On ImageNet-1k-LT using EDC with 50 images per class, ADSA improves tail-class accuracy by up to 11.8% and reaches 41.4% overall accuracy. The findings identify soft-label calibration as a practical intervention for making compact synthetic datasets more useful when the original data contain substantial class imbalance.
neurips-2025-rectifying-soft-label-entan.tldr: ADSA corrects intertwined soft-label biases to improve dataset distillation when training classes are unevenly represented.

paragraphs: River discharge forecasting depends on how water conditions evolve across connected locations over time. The paper argues that existing deep learning approaches in hydrology are largely local and underuse these spatial connections. RiverMamba targets global forecasting by modeling the spatial and temporal relationships within very large river networks.

The model is pretrained on long-term reanalysis data and uses efficient Mamba blocks to capture those relationships. Its forecast blocks incorporate ECMWF HRES weather forecasts, with spatiotemporal modeling accounting for inaccuracies in that input. RiverMamba predicts discharge and floods on a 0.05-degree grid with lead times of up to seven days, a range relevant to early warning.

The authors report reliable discharge predictions across lead times and floods with different return periods, including extreme events. Their analysis finds that RiverMamba surpasses both AI-based and physics-based models. These findings support the value of combining large-network relationships, historical pretraining, and forecast weather inputs. The contribution brings those elements together in a model intended to extend learning-based hydrological prediction to a global scale.
neurips-2025-rivermamba-a-state-space-mo.tldr: RiverMamba models large river networks across space and time to forecast global discharge and floods up to seven days ahead.

paragraphs: Safety behavior learned in static settings may fail to transfer to video, where the relevant context unfolds over time. SafeVid addresses this mismatch in video large multimodal models. Its central idea is to describe videos in detailed text, allowing language-model safety reasoning to help guide alignment for dynamic visual content.

The framework connects three components in a closed loop. First, it creates SafeVid-350K, a dataset containing 350,000 video-specific safety preference pairs. Second, it trains video models on those preferences using Direct Preference Optimization. Third, it evaluates the resulting behavior with SafeVidBench. Textual descriptions act as the bridge that enables rule-driven safety reasoning during this process.

Training with the preference dataset significantly improves safety on the new benchmark. The abstract reports improvements of up to 42.39% for models such as LLaVA-NeXT-Video. These results support using textual interpretation to transfer safety capabilities into video models. The contribution includes both an alignment procedure and the training and evaluation resources needed to study safety in the video settings considered.
neurips-2025-safevid-toward-safety-align.tldr: SafeVid uses detailed video descriptions to transfer textual safety reasoning into preference training for video multimodal models.

paragraphs: SceneDesigner addresses simultaneous control of multiple objects’ locations, sizes, and orientations in generated images. These attributes form the nine degrees of freedom considered by the paper. The challenge is to make detailed pose instructions reliable while maintaining image quality, particularly when several objects must be generated together.

The method adds a branched network to a pretrained model and supplies pose information through a camera-view representation called a CNOCS map. Its geometric interpretability supports more efficient and stable training. The authors also construct ObjectPose9D, combining diverse images with pose annotations. To address underrepresented poses, a second training stage uses a reward-based objective on rebalanced data.

During generation, Disentangled Object Sampling reduces missing objects and confusion between object concepts. Personalization weights also allow pose control for user-specific reference subjects. Qualitative and quantitative experiments report significant improvements in control and image quality over existing approaches. The overall design addresses pose representation, uneven training coverage, and multi-object generation as connected parts of the control problem.
neurips-2025-scenedesigner-controllable-.tldr: SceneDesigner combines geometric pose conditioning, rebalanced training, and specialized sampling to control multiple objects’ positions, sizes, and orientations.

paragraphs: Predicting drug-drug interactions is difficult when a drug has few known interaction examples. The paper argues that relying only on labeled interactions leaves useful information in unlabeled drug pairs unexplored. S²VM develops a self-supervised pretraining approach that learns from visual molecular structure and from the relationship between the two drugs in a pair.

The method blends visual fragments from both molecules into one input for joint encoding, then recovers molecule-specific visual information for each drug. This task incorporates structural details such as the relative positions and connectivity of functional substructures. Visual fragments serve as anchors for local spatial information, helping form richer representations of drug pairs from unlabeled examples.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on widely used benchmarks, with Macro-F1 improvements of 4.21% and 3.31%. Additional experiments and theoretical analysis support effectiveness for drugs with few examples and for novel drugs. The findings suggest that jointly learning visual structural context from unlabeled pairs can strengthen interaction prediction when known interaction data provide limited coverage.
neurips-2025-self-supervised-blending-st.tldr: S²VM learns from blended molecular images to improve drug-interaction prediction, including for drugs with limited or novel interaction data.

paragraphs: Sparta Alignment trains a group of language models through repeated competitions. The motivation is that a single model can have limited response diversity and biased self-evaluation. In each iteration, two models answer one instruction, while the remaining models judge their responses. This brings several models’ expertise into both answer generation and evaluation.

Judgments are combined through an adapted Elo-style reputation system. Models gain or lose influence as judges according to their own competition results. The winning and losing responses become a preference pair, and every participating model learns from the collected preferences at the end of the iteration. Competition therefore supplies a shared training signal for the whole group.

Experiments report better results than the initial models and four self-alignment baselines on 10 of 12 tasks and datasets, with an average improvement of 7.0%. Further analysis finds stronger generalization to unseen tasks and more logical, direct, informative outputs. These findings support collective preference learning as a way to make use of differences in participating models’ expertise.
neurips-2025-sparta-alignment-collective.tldr: Sparta Alignment improves multiple language models through peer-judged competitions that generate shared preference-training data.

paragraphs: Massively parallel simulation lets reinforcement learning agents collect experience quickly. With short rollouts between policy updates, however, synchronized environment resets can make training batches change sharply in the kinds of states they contain. The paper identifies this reset-induced nonstationarity as a source of distorted learning signals and unstable training in that setting.

Staggered resets spread environment initialization and resetting across different points in the task horizon. As a result, training batches contain a more uniform distribution of visited states. The intervention changes the timing of experience collection. The authors use toy environments to characterize circumstances in which this timing adjustment can produce substantial benefits.

They then apply the technique to challenging, high-dimensional robotics environments. Reported gains include higher sample efficiency, faster convergence in elapsed time, and stronger final performance. Staggered resets also scale better as the number of parallel environments increases. These findings show that organizing the temporal composition of training batches can help turn additional simulation capacity into more effective on-policy learning.
neurips-2025-staggered-environment-reset.tldr: Spreading environment resets across the task horizon stabilizes training batches and improves massively parallel on-policy reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Medical image prognosis predicts how a condition may progress over time, including when an event may occur. The paper examines fairness in this time-to-event setting, an area it identifies as receiving less attention than diagnosis tasks such as classification and segmentation. FairTTE provides a framework for systematically evaluating disparities in these prognostic predictions.

The framework covers multiple imaging modalities and time-to-event outcomes, combining prediction methods with fairness algorithms. It also uses causal analysis to identify and quantify distinct sources of bias in the underlying datasets. This connects evaluation of model disparities with an investigation of the data-generating factors that may contribute to them.

The large-scale evaluation finds pervasive bias across imaging modalities and limited mitigation from current fairness methods. It reports a strong association between underlying bias sources and model disparities, with fairness becoming harder to maintain under distribution shifts. The findings motivate approaches that address multiple sources of bias together and make robustness to changing data conditions part of prognostic fairness evaluation.
neurips-2025-the-boundaries-of-fair-ai-i.tldr: FairTTE finds widespread bias and limited effectiveness of current fairness methods in medical image prognosis, especially under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks build representations through local message passing, while visual perception can recognize an overall arrangement at once. This paper investigates whether vision models offer a useful route to understanding graph structure. On established benchmarks, they perform comparably to graph neural networks but learn in noticeably different ways, motivating a closer examination of what those benchmarks actually measure.

The authors introduce GraphAbstract to isolate holistic structural abilities that existing evaluations can mix with domain-specific features. Its tasks involve recognizing organizational patterns, detecting symmetry, assessing connectivity strength, and identifying critical elements. The emphasis is on properties of the graph’s overall organization, making the benchmark a focused test of global topological understanding.

In these evaluations, vision models significantly outperform graph neural networks on tasks requiring holistic understanding and generalize across graph sizes. The tested graph neural networks struggle with global abstraction and deteriorate as graphs grow. The findings support exploring vision models for graph tasks dominated by global patterns and suggest a useful direction for developing graph foundation models.
neurips-2025-the-underappreciated-power-.tldr: GraphAbstract reveals strong vision-model performance on global graph structure, including better generalization across graph sizes than the tested GNNs.

paragraphs: Blind image quality assessment predicts quality without a reference image at evaluation time. Synthetic training data can help overcome limited labels, but models trained on them often transfer poorly. This paper observes that their learned representations form discrete clusters: high-quality images group around reference content, while low-quality images group by distortion type, hindering quality regression.

The authors trace this problem to the synthetic data distribution and propose SynDR-IQA to reshape it. Guided by theoretical analysis of diversity and redundancy, the framework increases diverse content while preserving the content distribution. It also reduces the density of crowded clusters by downsampling redundant examples. These operations adjust the mix of training samples used to learn quality representations.

Experiments evaluate transfer from synthetic data to authentic distortions, algorithmic distortions, and other synthetic datasets. Results support the effectiveness of the distribution changes across all three settings. The contribution identifies how synthetic examples are distributed as a practical target for improving generalization, connecting representation clustering with concrete choices about which examples to add or remove.
neurips-2025-towards-syn-to-real-iqa-a-n.tldr: SynDR-IQA improves synthetic-data generalization for image quality assessment by increasing content diversity and reducing redundant clusters.

paragraphs: Uni-RL develops one model-free reinforcement learning formulation for online learning, offline learning, and transitions between them. It extends Implicit Value Regularization by replacing a constraint tied specifically to dataset behavior with one defined relative to a reference policy. The reference is the target policy online and the behavior policy offline.

An iteratively refined behavior policy addresses the excessive restriction that arises when applying the original framework directly online. Value learning provides an implicit trust-region-style update while remaining off-policy. Uni-RL also unifies policy extraction, estimating an in-sample policy gradient using actions from the reference policy. The paper provides theoretical guarantees of reduced value-estimation error and greater performance improvement over that reference.

Across standard benchmarks, the authors report stronger online sample efficiency than the compared off-policy and on-policy methods. Offline, improved policy extraction outperforms IVR while retaining in-sample learning benefits. During offline-to-online adaptation, the method exceeds both constrained and unconstrained approaches. These findings support the reference-policy formulation as a way to balance stability and adaptation across different sources of experience.
neurips-2025-uni-rl-unifying-online-and-.tldr: Uni-RL uses reference-policy-based value regularization and policy extraction to unify online, offline, and offline-to-online reinforcement learning.
